stories.title: Performance enhancement of electrohydrodynamic thruster using sub unit electrode configuration
stories.description: Electrohydrodynamic (EHD) propulsion has garnered significant interest as a lightweight and silent thrust generation technology, owing to its lack of moving parts and low vibration characteristics. However, enhancing the thrust output and energy efficiency of EHD thrusters remains a key challenge. This study introduces a novel thrust enhancement electrode configuration that incorporates a sub unit for an EHD propulsion system. Experimental results demonstrate that the introduction of the sub unit substantially increases thrust generation compared with the conventional electrode system without a sub unit. At an applied voltage of 22 kV, the conventional configuration generates a thrust of 50.23 mN, whereas the sub unit electrode system achieves 64.09 mN, representing an approximate 27.59% increase in thrust. To further enhance thrust generation, an additional structure, termed the sub unit plus, is implemented beneath the original sub unit electrode system. This enhanced configuration optimizes aerodynamic interactions within the investigated range, resulting in a thrust output of 68.70 mN. The sub unit plus electrode system delivers an additional 7.19% increase in thrust over the sub unit configuration alone, and a total improvement of 36.77% relative to the conventional system. These results indicate an engineering trade-off between maximizing absolute thrust and maintaining thrust to power ratio of the configuration. Overall, the incorporation of sub unit structures is crucial in enhancing thrust output. The proposed design strategy provides a promising pathway for improving thrust performance in EHD propulsion systems and provides valuable insights for the development of higher thrust output EHD thrusters.

stories.title: Comparative analysis of long-term electricity load forecasting using machine learning and meta-heuristic-optimized hybrid architectures
stories.description: Accurate long-term electricity peak load forecasting is essential for modern power system growth, reliability, and effective infrastructure planning. There is no single model for load forecasting that works for all electric utilities, as it can differ from region to region and among customer types. This paper presents a strong, data-driven approach that uses historical economic and demographic data from 2016 to 2025 to predict electrical power loads over a 10-year period for Adigrat city. Using advanced Pandas techniques for imputation of missing data and customer class correlation analysis to identify strongly related attributes, data pretreatment was meticulously carried out. In order to tackle the forecasting problem, we compare our proposed novel hybrid framework Particle Swarm Optimized (PSO) LSTM-NN with Machine Learning (ML) regression, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), LSTM-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and a hybrid LSTM-(NN)-Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model. To address potential out-of-sample scaling issues and risks of performance drop with standard standalone deep learners, we introduce an intelligent input-combination conditional feature selection engine. The uniqueness of this research comes from creating a highly robust, customer-focused framework for long-term load forecasting (LTLF) which combines tailored demographic analysis, automated handling of missing data, and an improved hybrid deep learning structure. This work primarily contributes a stringent preprocessing pipeline (featuring missing data mitigation and multivariate correlation analysis) alongside empirical proof that the LSTM-NN-PSO model delivers superior accuracy and extended stability when projecting intricate macroeconomic variables across a 10-year period.
